verdicts.GOOD: the visible difference is the difference the setting makes, and it is readable at the size a tooltip shows it
verdicts.WEAK: on the right subject but ambiguous, undirected, or too faint to read -- or, for the two marked SHOWS THE WRONG THING, not on the subject at all

method: Every animation was WATCHED: all stored frames of the SHIPPED GIF rendered as a contact sheet and read against that setting's own text in spacr/settings.py. A machine cannot make these 94 judgements; it can only keep the record honest.

The pixel metric is a floor, never a verdict. It is blind in both directions: cytoplasm scores 13.5%, 13th highest of 94, and shows nothing of its setting, while crop_mode scores 1.8% and is one of the clearest in the set.

The four border animations are measured, not judged by eye, with spacr.setting_animations.measure_border_object_removal: it reads the well edge off the DRAWN rule rather than the generator's own touches flag, and compares two frames at the same zoom rather than frame 0, which is zoomed out. All four report crossing=2 interior=0.
Two sessions audited this concurrently on 2026-08-18. This record is the union of both: an animation is WEAK if either pass found it weak.

FIXED 2026-08-20. The root cause recorded below was exact: painter.line(..., fill_closed=True) was the LAST call and painted an opaque polygon over all three compartments (1988 blue / 1028 teal / 300 magenta before it, 0 / 0 / 0 after). Passing fill_closed=False alone would have left three compartments floating on a fill, which is a picture of a cell rather than of this setting -- so the ORDER is the fix: the cytoplasm region is filled FIRST and the compartments are drawn on top, where they read as punched out of it, which is what the setting does. The fill was also dimmed from 0.35..0.90 to 0.18..0.48 -- a near-white slab is not something a half-width outline can be seen against -- and the compartments are drawn at width 1.1 because here they are the subject rather than context. Measured on the regenerated GIF: at least 89 nucleus pixels in EVERY one of the 18 frames, against 0 before.

FIXED 2026-08-20. The subject was already right -- a poorly-fitting doubled mask beside a clean one is discarded -- and the DIRECTION was backwards by implication, which is worse than a faint animation. flow_threshold is counter-intuitive (LOWERING it discards more masks) while every animation in this set runs off -> on, so the frame where the ragged mask vanishes was also the frame a viewer reads as 'the setting went up'. Nothing in the drawing said which way the value moved, so the viewer supplied the only reading available and it was the wrong one. A track below the masks now EMPTIES as the discard happens -- measured: the fill reaches x=274 at action 0 and x=169 at action 1 -- so the value and the consequence move in the same direction instead of opposite ones.

FIXED 2026-08-20. Three changes, each about the same thing -- a split is only a split if you can see the gap. (1) THE HALVES MOVE APART instead of appearing where they will end up: they start at the original's centre and separate as the action runs, which is what a watershed DOES. (2) THEY END 100 px APART rather than 60, so two 32-wide glyphs have clear ground between them. (3) THE CROSSFADE RAMPS OVERLAP -- out over 0..0.6, in over 0.4..1.0 -- because a clean hand-off at 0.5 left a frame with NOTHING on it (measured: left 0, centre 0, right 0), and a blank frame reads as a broken animation rather than an unclear one. Plus the watershed LINE is drawn: a watershed is a boundary, and drawing it is the difference between 'two things now' and 'here is where one became two'. Measured on the regenerated GIF: 18 frames, none near-blank, and 4 separate ink groups in the final frame where the mush was one.

FIXED 2026-08-20. The subject was right -- a brightness ramp across five objects responding to the setting -- and the animation BRIGHTENED while raising Signal_to_noise raises the normalisation ceiling and makes things DIMMER. Same class as the flow thresholds and filed the same milder way: a picture that moves the wrong way is not undirected, it is directed wrongly, and a viewer will read it. The ramp dims now, and THE DIMMEST LOSES MOST -- each object's fall is scaled by its own base, so the faintest fades toward nothing while the brightest merely dulls, which is what raising the ceiling does to a field. The same track the flow thresholds use sits below, FILLING rather than emptying, because here the value goes up as the picture goes down. Measured on the regenerated GIF: 18 frames, brightest at index 0 (3002 bright pixels) and dimmest at index 11 (2563) -- and that is with the gauge ADDING ink as it fills.

FIXED 2026-08-20. THE CONTROL WAS MISSING: every object in the frame split, so the animation showed the CONSEQUENCE of the setting and nothing about what DECIDES it -- a viewer could not tell whether it splits everything or only some things, which is the only question a threshold setting raises. The audit prescribed the fix and it is the one taken: draw an object that is NOT split, rather than drawing an intensity valley the setting does not use (settings.py records the split as purely GEOMETRIC for pathogen). A large object on the left comes apart, a small one on the right is left alone, and both are on screen the whole time -- the difference between them IS the setting. The cut is drawn where the halves part, because a split has a place it happens and showing it is the difference between 'two now' and 'cut here'. Measured: the control's ink is 7391 pixels in EVERY frame while the splitting side moves 9655 -> 14448 -> 12997.
